summary: Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1994). After posts at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, and King's College London, she was appointed Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale University in 2006.

Verrier Elwin worked in Indology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Dean Close School and Merton College (~1921–1926), and served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India (~1946–1949).

Vesna Wallace works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley and held posts at the University of Oxford (-2010) and UC Santa Barbara, where she is attested as Professor, Department Chair, and Distinguished University Professor.

Victor Chan is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at the University of Chicago. In 2005, he founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education and was attested as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

Victor Forte works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Temple University (-2004) and was attested in 2007 as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Dartmouth, the University of Washington, SOAS, and Harvard under Patrick Hanan and James Robert Hightower, he taught at Harvard (~1976–1979) before becoming Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Victor Henry was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the University of Douai (~1880–1887), the University of Lille (~1887–1889), and the University of Paris, where he was appointed professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar in 1888.

Victor Lieberman is a historian who earned his BA at Yale (~1963–1967) and his PhD at SOAS (~1971–1976). In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History and Professor of Asian and Comparative History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Turner worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at University College London and the University of Manchester, holding posts at Manchester (~1955–1963), Cornell (1963), the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was attested as Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (1929–1944) and as retired Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Vidya Dehejia works in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at St. Xavier's College, Newnham College, and the University of Cambridge (PhD ~1963–1968), later holding positions at the Smithsonian Institution and Columbia University (associate professor 1982; endowed chair 2002).

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya and earned degrees from Allahabad and Gorakhpur. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1977), K. M. Institute (~1977–1986), and as vice-chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).

Vijayalakshmi Mani works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Vilhelm Thomsen was a Danish linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen (PhD 1859–1869). He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1869), associate professor (1875), and professor (1887–1913), later serving as President of the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters (1909).

Vinay Lal is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1987–1992) and became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at UCLA around 1993.

Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Charles University (~1903–1907) under Moriz Winternitz and Josef Zubatý. He later served on the faculty at Charles University from ~1918 to 1953.

Vincent Arthur Smith was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate from Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) and later held posts at the University of Oxford, including Curator of the Indian Institute (~1910–1920).

Vincent Eltschinger works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and became Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2015.

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997). He worked at the CNRS (~1998–2012) before becoming Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.
